rationale: The reviewer found that the random pair split puts every test protein in training (140/140 pairs) and that a per-protein label-rate baseline with no sequence information reaches AUROC 0.795 against the model's 0.790. Their remedy was a protein-disjoint split plus a degree baseline. Their other points (homology, small test set, no permutation null, possible artifacts in the negatives) are generic or speculative, not separately established important flaws.
